titulo: Stay a while: the inbox hour
caption: YouTube only (a medio in 16:9, no Short and no Reel). What goes out is the YouTube title and the description.
descripcion:
A quiet 11-minute stretch for the replies still waiting in the inbox. No voice and no lecture. A clock runs from 4:46 p.m. on a Thursday, short cards come and go, the afternoon sun sinks slowly in the window, and a drawn character, Cella, sits next to the desk and does not move. Open the oldest one, answer in two sentences, and go as slow as you like. Leave the video on or off whenever you want.

Somebody still has replies to write tonight.

Cella is an AI character. Nobody is on the other end of this video: it is a clock, some cards and music made with code.

Choose friction.
alt: An 11-minute video in 16:9 with no voice. A room late on a Thursday afternoon: a wooden desk with a laptop showing an inbox of a few lines and a mug, a window with the sun going down slowly, a wall clock, and Cella, a small blocky black figure with two round white eyes and no hands, sitting very still next to the desk. A clock in the corner starts at 4:46 PM and runs one second per second, and never reaches five o'clock. The lines on the laptop screen get fewer as the video goes on. Every 40 to 50 seconds a short card replaces the last one, such as Five o'clock is close, Stay a while, Open the oldest one, Two sentences is a reply, Not sure yet, A date is an answer, Thanks is a whole reply and Done is a good size. It ends on For whoever still has replies to write, and Choose friction.
